hints: Focus on the structure needed for the iodoform test, not just whether it is an aldehyde, ketone or alcohol.
Check butanone and ethanal first, both contain the key $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group or the very closely related $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ group.
Remember that alkaline iodine is oxidising, so think about what propan-2-ol can be turned into in the test tube before it reacts further.
walkthrough:
**Recall what gives a positive iodoform test**

This pale yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ is the classic test for one special group. You need a methyl carbonyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, or a group that can easily form it.

General positive unit:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ or } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$$

**Test compounds 1 and 2**

Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is a methyl ketone, so it reacts directly.

Ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. It is the only aldehyde that contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$-like unit, so it also reacts directly. So 1 and 2 are correct.

**Test compound 3, the tricky one**

Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It is a secondary alcohol with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group.

Under the alkaline oxidising conditions, $\text{I}_2$ in $\text{NaOH}$, it is first oxidised to propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, which is a methyl ketone and then gives $\text{CHI}_3$. So 3 is also correct.

**Put it together**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all give the pale yellow precipitate, the combination with all three is the right choice.

options.A: Correct. Butanone is a methyl ketone, ethanal contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, and propan-2-ol contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ which is oxidised in situ to a methyl ketone. All three give $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2. Students choose this when they remember methyl ketones and ethanal but forget that methyl secondary alcohols like propan-2-ol are also oxidised and then give a positive result.
options.C: Incorrect. This option leaves out butanone. Students choose this if they think only ethanal and alcohols react, forgetting that butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a perfect example of a methyl ketone.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only butanone. Students choose this if they think only ketones give the test, forgetting the special case of ethanal and the oxidisable $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ alcohols.
